basis: Intestinal egg-induced inflammation characterizes infection; functionally significant hepatosplenic disease generally affects <30%.

decisions.hepatic: none: functionally significant hepatic disease generally affects <30%; hepatic egg deposition alone does not establish impaired function.

basis: Encephalopathy is brain dysfunction caused by liver disease or portosystemic shunting; it does not itself damage the liver.

decisions.hepatic: none: hepatic dysfunction is the underlying cause, usually a separately diagnosed liver disease; encephalopathy itself affects the brain.

basis: Developmental impairment, hypogonadism and skeletal anomalies define syndrome; dental defects 80-99%. Renal, ocular and ear abnormalities 30-79% omitted by cap.

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: characteristic skeletal malformations, particularly radioulnar synostosis and joint abnormalities, are defining components of this syndrome.

basis: Polyendocrinopathy and progressive ataxia define syndrome; dental abnormalities occur in 80-99%. Short stature and finger deviation do not establish functional skeletal damage.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: short stature and finger deviation (80-99%) are reported, but skeletal dysfunction, destructive disease or fixed contractures are not established.

basis: Copper-metabolism disorder causing axonal neuropathy; muscle atrophy and ocular motor findings occur in 30-79% but do not establish direct muscle or eye injury.

decisions.ocular: none: ptosis and exotropia (30-79%) can reflect motor neuropathy; direct damage to ocular structures is not established.
decisions.musculoskeletal: none: weakness and atrophy (30-79%) accompany chronic denervation; primary muscle pathology or fixed skeletal damage is not established.

basis: Progressive cerebellar degeneration, sensorineural deafness and optic atrophy are defining features; hearing impairment and optic atrophy occur in 80-99%.

decisions.ocular: primary: optic atrophy is explicitly part of the disease definition and occurs in 80-99%; the optic nerve belongs to the ocular axis.

basis: Luft disease is a mitochondrial myopathy with uncoupled oxidative phosphorylation causing hypermetabolism and skeletal muscle dysfunction.

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: this is Luft mitochondrial myopathy; defective oxidative phosphorylation in skeletal muscle and muscle dysfunction characterize the disease.

basis: Craniofacial, ear and limbal abnormalities define spectrum; renal malformations occur in 30-79%. Neurodevelopmental delay (30-79%) omitted at cap, prioritizing structural renal defects.

decisions.renal: involved: renal malformations occur in 30-79%; structural renal involvement is retained within the four-axis cap.
decisions.neurologic: none under cap: neurodevelopmental delay is reported in 30-79%, but structural renal abnormalities are prioritized after the three defining axes.

basis: Neurodegeneration, retinal dystrophy and deafness define syndrome; fixed limb contractures occur in 1/1 assessed and cubitus valgus in 2/2, supporting structural involvement.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: fixed limb contractures (1/1 assessed) and cubitus valgus (2/2) establish structural impairment beyond weakness; frequency estimates have very small denominators.

basis: Congenital fusion of the jaws and oral tissues defines syngnathia, directly restricting mouth opening; dysostosis ancestry supports skeletal involvement.

decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: syngnathia is congenital fusion within the oral cavity that directly restricts mouth opening; the mouth is included in the gastrointestinal axis.
